transcript:
Meeting header: 2027-11-29 16:00 UTC | Duration: 45m
Attendees: Avery Chen (Redwood AE), Samir Patel (Redwood SE), Maya Ortiz (Redwood CSM), Emily Carter (Montclair Product), Dr. Marcus Hill (Montclair CTO), Aisha Khan (Montclair Head of IT), Ravi Menon (Montclair Security)

Summary: Quick intros, then dive into onboarding plan and security. Slight background noise on customer line at ~00:42.

[00:00] Avery Chen: hey everyone thanks for joining, um this is a quick kickoff, i'm avery chen, i'll be your ae, samir here is our se, maya is cs, uh can you do quick intros from your side?
[00:12] Emily Carter: yes hi emily carter, director of product at montclair, we're leading the integration and product acceptance criteria, short and sweet.
[00:20] Dr. Marcus Hill: marcus hill, cto, i'll own technical sign off and performance requirements.
[00:26] Aisha Khan: aisha here, head of it, i'll handle networking, sso and ops.
[00:30] Ravi Menon: ravi, security, will be looking at compliance and audit logs.
[00:35] Samir Patel: great thanks, so high level today i want to cover the onboarding timeline, what success looks like, and the three deployment models real quick \u001f hosted api, dedicated and private/vpc on prem. we'll also flag any immediate blockers, right?
[00:50] Emily Carter: sounds good, timeline \u001f we're hoping pilot in jan, production q1, is that realistic?
[00:56] Avery Chen: yep that's what we've seen with similar customers, pilot in 6-8 weeks if we get staging access and the network details, production by end of q1 assuming no major security blockers.
[01:10] Dr. Marcus Hill: for us the big metric is latency 95th pct under 350ms for interactive use, and cost per throughput to be evaluated. also data residency, we need logs to not leave region.
[01:26] Samir Patel: understood, latency is something we tune with batching, kv cache, and the right model/quantization. just to flag, our dedicated pools give you stronger throughput guarantees and predictable economics; private gives you full control for residency but requires more setup.
[01:45] Aisha Khan: on private deployment, what's required for network? we have a strict firewall and internal subnets.
[01:50] Samir Patel: we'll need VPC peering or private link depending on cloud, open ports for control plane if using managed private, and we often ask for a bastion or jump host for initial setup. also prometheus metrics endpoints for health.
[02:05] Aisha Khan: okay can you send a template of the network topology you need?
[02:09] Samir Patel: yes i'll send a detailed runbook.
[02:12] Emily Carter: security \u001f ravi will want SOC 2 and key management. do you support customer KMS?
[02:18] Maya Ortiz: yes redwood supports customer-managed keys (kms/hsm) for private and dedicated; hosted can be integrated but there's a short onboarding step for key rotation.
[02:27] Ravi Menon: also need audit logs, retention options and who has access \u001f can we get a log sample?
[02:33] Avery Chen: we'll share our audit log schema and retention configs, plus the SOC2 whitepaper and our pen test summary.
[02:40] Emily Carter: great, also wondering about SSO, our okta team will need saml metadata.
[02:45] Samir Patel: yep we support SAML/SSO and SCIM for provisioning; please share metadata and we'll configure.
[02:52] Dr. Marcus Hill: on performance testing, can we run a benchmark with our typical prompt mix? we have a mix of short queries and longer context generative requests.
[02:58] Samir Patel: absolutely \u001f we usually run a 2-stage benchmark: synthetic throughput to validate latency/throughput, then replay a sample of customer requests to test model quality and cost. we can run that on staging dedicated or hosted depending on preference.
[03:12] Emily Carter: i'd prefer staging dedicated so we can see production-like throughput, but if that's extra cost we'd consider hosted first.
[03:20] Avery Chen: we can quote staging dedicated for a short burst vs hosted; samir will share numbers.
[03:27] Aisha Khan: regarding data, does the hosted api persist prompts or are they ephemeral?
[03:32] Maya Ortiz: by default hosted retains logs for a short period for troubleshooting; we have options for no retention or for customers to opt into extended retention. private/dedicated gives you more control.
[03:42] [audio artifact] (brief static)
[03:45] Ravi Menon: one more security note, we may need a third-party pen test to validate the deployment pre-prod. any issues with that?
[03:50] Samir Patel: no problem, we've supported many customer-led pen tests; we'll provide scope and guidelines.
[03:57] Emily Carter: timeline recap: we want staging access this week ideally, run initial bench next week, then pilot in jan.
[04:06] Avery Chen: ok so actions: we'll send onboarding guide and staging creds, samir will schedule deep technical session, maya will share SOC2 and security docs, customer to share network diagram and SAML metadata.
[04:22] Dr. Marcus Hill: for the bench, to be clear, we expect 95th pct latency under 350ms for a 512 token average, is that feasible?
[04:32] Samir Patel: with the right model variant and quantization yes, we can be in that neighborhood; we should validate on the replay. some phrasing \u001f if you need lower p95 we'd recommend dedicated with certain kernel optimizations.
[04:46] Emily Carter: ok, and pricing \u001f can you send a pilot pricing estimate?
[04:50] Avery Chen: yes we'll include pilot pricing, dedicated pricing tiers, and private deployment estimates.
[04:56] Aisha Khan: one practical question \u001f who on your side will be the day-to-day technical contact?
[04:59] Samir Patel: i'll be the primary se for day-to-day and ava support will be the csm, maya is on this thread.
[05:08] Emily Carter: great thanks, any other questions?
[05:11] Ravi Menon: none from security at moment.
[05:13] Dr. Marcus Hill: no more from my side.
[05:15] Avery Chen: ok final recap \u001f we'll send materials and schedule deep-dive; agreed due dates in action items. thanks everyone, we'll follow up in email.
[05:25] Emily Carter: thanks all, bye.

End of transcript.
